The '''2022 Brent London Borough Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022. All 57 members of [[Brent London Borough Council]] were to be elected. The elections took place alongside [[2022 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]] and [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|elections to local authorities across the United Kingdom]].

In the [[2018 Brent London Borough Council election|previous election in 2018]], the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] maintained its control of the council, winning 60 out of the 63 seats with the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] forming the council opposition with the remaining three seats. The 2022 election took place under new election boundaries, which reduced the number of councillors to 57.

== Background ==

=== History ===
[[File:Brent_London_UK_local_election_2018_map.svg|thumb|Result of the 2018 borough election]]
The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police and fire.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref>

Since its formation, Brent has been variously under [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] control, [[no overall control]] and [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] control. Only Labour, Conservative and [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrat]] councillors have been elected to the council. The council has had an overall Labour majority since the [[2010 Brent London Borough Council election|2010 election]], in which Labour won 40 seats, the Liberal Democrats won 17 and the Conservatives won six. The Liberal Democrats lost all but one of their seats in the [[2014 Brent London Borough Council election|2014 election]] before losing their final seat in the most recent election in [[2018 Brent London Borough Council election|2018]]. The 2018 result saw Labour win 60 seats with 57.6% of the overall vote, and the Conservatives win three with 22.5% of the overall vote. The Liberal Democrats received 12.6% of votes across the borough and the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] received 5.6% of the vote, but neither won any seats. The incumbent leader of the council is Muhammed Butt, who has held that position since 2014.

=== Council term ===
Michael Pavey, a Labour councillor for Barnhill ward, resigned in November 2019, citing family reasons.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Raffray|first=Nathalie|date=2019-11-26|title=Barnhill councillor Michael Pavey resigns from Brent Council citing 'family reasons'|url=https://www.kilburntimes.co.uk/news/labour-s-michael-pavey-resigns-from-brent-council-3829238|access-date=2021-09-21|website=Kilburn Times|language=en-UK}}</ref> In May 2016, while serving as deputy leader of the council, he had unsuccessfully challenged Butt for the leadership of the council.<ref name=":0" /> Later in 2016 he resigned from the council's cabinet because he disagreed with Butt about how to implement cuts.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Councillor resigns after seven years of service|url=https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/18064399.barnhill-councillor-michael-pavey-steps-role-brent-council/|access-date=2021-09-21|website=Harrow Times|date=28 November 2019 |language=en}}</ref> Another Labour councillor for the same ward, Sarah Marquis, resigned days later, citing family and personal reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Raffray|first=Nathalie|date=2019-12-04|title=Sarah Marquis stands down from Barnhill ward within days of fellow councillor Michael Pavey|url=https://www.kilburntimes.co.uk/news/barnhill-ward-sarah-marquis-resigns-3829626|access-date=2021-09-21|website=Kilburn Times|language=en-UK}}</ref> A Labour councillor for Wembley Central ward, Luke Patterson, resigned in the same month citing personal reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Third councillor resigns within a week|url=https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/18085739.luke-patterson-resigns-brent-council-following-two-former-colleagues/|access-date=2021-09-21|website=Harrow Times|date=6 December 2019 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Raffray|first=Nathalie|date=2019-12-10|title=Brent Council resignation: Wembley Central councillor is third Labour representative to stand down|url=https://www.kilburntimes.co.uk/news/wembley-central-luke-patterson-resigns-3830184|access-date=2021-09-21|website=Kilburn Times|language=en-UK}}</ref> By-elections to replace all three, in addition to James Allie, a Labour councillor for Alperton who resigned, were held on 23 January 2020.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Raffray|first=Nathalie|date=2020-01-08|title=Labour suspends by-election candidate amid investigation into tweets|url=https://www.kilburntimes.co.uk/news/labour-brent-by-election-candidate-chetan-harpale-suspended-3831770|access-date=2021-09-21|website=Kilburn Times|language=en-UK}}</ref> Allie was reportedly suspended from the party.<ref name=":2" /> The Labour candidate to replace Allie, Chetan Harpale, was suspended from his party during the campaign to investigate alleged Islamophobia.<ref name=":2"/> Harpale lost the election, with the Liberal Democrat candidate Anton Georgiou being elected.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Lib Dems return to council following by-election win as Labour holds three seats|url=https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/18184681.new-councillors-elected-brent-council-2020-by-election/|access-date=2021-09-21|website=Harrow Times|date=24 January 2020 |language=en}}</ref> The other three by-elections were all held by Labour on reduced majorities.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=Baston|first=Lewis|date=2020-01-24|title=Brent: Big by-election swings against Labour as Lib Dems make gain|url=https://www.onlondon.co.uk/brent-big-by-election-swings-against-labour-as-lib-dems-make-gain/|access-date=2021-09-21|website=OnLondon|language=en-GB}}</ref>

In 2021, a Labour councillor for Brondesbury Park, Kieron Gill, resigned, declining to explain his reasons.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|last=Raffray|first=Nathalie|date=2021-05-05|title=Kilburn councillor resigns from Labour Group|url=https://www.kilburntimes.co.uk/news/kilburn-councillor-abdi-abdizarak-resigns-7947888|access-date=2021-09-21|website=Kilburn Times|language=en-UK}}</ref> Earlier in 2021 he had been the only Labour councillor to abstain on the council budget.<ref name="Raffray">{{Cite web|last=Raffray|first=Nathalie|date=2021-03-24|title=Brondesbury Park councillor resigns|url=https://www.kilburntimes.co.uk/news/brondesbury-park-councillor-kieron-gill-resigns-7847850|access-date=2021-09-21|website=Kilburn Times|language=en-UK}}</ref> The by-election was held on 6 May 2021, on the same date as the [[2021 London mayoral election|2021 London mayoral]] and [[2021 London Assembly election|London Assembly elections]].<ref name="Raffray"/> The Labour candidate, Gwen Grahl, was elected.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ldrs|first=Adam Shaw|date=2021-05-07|title=Labour wins Brondesbury Park in tightly contested by-election|url=https://www.kilburntimes.co.uk/news/labour-wins-brondesbury-park-by-election-7955950|access-date=2021-09-21|website=Kilburn Times|language=en-UK}}</ref> Earlier that week, the Labour candidate Abdirazak Abdi resigned from the Labour group to sit as an independent councillor.<ref name=":4" />

Along with most other London boroughs, Brent was subject to a boundary review ahead of the 2022 election. The [[Local Government Boundary Commission for England]] concluded that the council should have 57 seats, a reduction of six, and produced new election boundaries following a period of consultation.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=LGBCE {{!}} Brent {{!}} LGBCE Site|url=http://www.lgbce.org.uk/all-reviews/greater-london/greater-london/brent|access-date=2021-09-21|website=www.lgbce.org.uk|language=en}}</ref> The new boundaries comprise thirteen three-councillor wards and nine two-councillor wards.<ref name=":5" />

== Electoral process ==
Brent, like other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years. The previous election took place in 2018. The election took place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors had as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected.

All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over were entitled to vote in the election. People who lived at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, were entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref> Voting in-person at polling stations took place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters were able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election.<ref name=":1" />

==Changes 2022-2026==

===Affiliation changes===
5 Labour MPs defected to the Green Party: Harbi Farah and Mary Mitchell, who represent Welsh Harp, Iman Ahmadi Moghaddam, who represents Wembley Park, Tony Ethapemi, who represents Stonebridge and Erica Gbajumo, who represents Brondesbury Park.<ref>{{cite web |title=Labour hit by Brent Councillor defections to Green Party |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/crl94n0wy32o|website=BBC}}</ref>
